findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine in the kitchen would not register sanitizer on either the inspector’s or facility’s test strips. Employees conducted troubleshooting on the equipment and the machine began functioning correctly prior to the inspector leaving. Ensure that the sanitizers in the facility are functioning correctly at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location.

A container labeled “seafood utensils” at a prep station was observed with standing water and floating debris in the bottom of the container. A nearby employee stated that it should be for clean utensils. The employee was shown and moved the container to dish for cleaning. Ensure that all food contact utensils are maintained clean and protected from contamination until use.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Opened containers of milk and buttermilk are observed without date marking in the walk in cooler. The PIC indicated that they were likely opened last week and discarded them to correct the violation. Ensure that all TCS foods are date marked once opened and discarded at the end of the seventh day.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area was without paper towels. The PIC was asked about paper towels and then replaced them during this inspection to correct. Ensure that all hand sinks are properly supplied at all times to promote good hand washing practices.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inside of the spout for the soda gun at the left side of the bar has a black substance built up. The PIC was shown and cleaned the item during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are cleaned often enough to prevent soilage.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A).

A pan of portioned cooked spaghetti in the walk in cooler has a date marking of 7/17/25. Today is day 13 when the items should have been used or discarded by the end of day seven. The PIC checked the bags and agreed that they were old and discarded them during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that TCS foods are used or discarded by the end of day seven where the day of preparation is day one.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(B) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (B) Except as specified in (E) - (G) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and PACKAGED by a FOOD PROCESSING PLANT shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and if the FOOD is held for more than 24 hours.

A gallon of milk in the walk in cooler is observed partially used. The PIC indicated that it had been opened approximately 5 days ago. Education was conducted and a date placed on the container to correct. Ensure that these items are given date markings if they are going to be at the facility longer than 24 hours and used or discarded prior to the end of the 7th day.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

The shelves in the walk in cooler are observed rusted and in need of repair. This can come in many forms but needs to have an end result of a smooth and easily cleanable surface. Repair/replace prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. 

Two of the three CFPMs at the facility are unable to show an allergen training certificate during this inspection. They are instructed to complete allergen training prior to the next routine inspection and maintain copies of the certificate at the facility moving forward.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Inspector observed three employees with personal drinks in the kitchen. The facility manager talked to the employees. One of the drinks had a lid and a straw and was down low as required. The other two were without lids or straws and improperly stored.  

(A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed the soda nozzles at the wait station to be soiled. Also the nozzle of the water dispenser at the wait station near the Liquor closet is soiled with mineral deposits. Clean and maintain these items clean. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: Live roaches are observed in the back corner of the south server station. The facility recently switched pest control companies. The new company paperwork states that they are on monthly service. Inspector highly suggests more frequent service and monitoring to eliminate pests from the facility. Follow up will be conducted in 10 days.

PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.13: Inspector observed the base cove in the back right corner of the south server station with the pest issue to have base cove that is pulled away from the wall and a gap where the roaches are congregating. Clean and seal this area to deny the pests a place to live. 

(A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple drain flies at the bar during this inspection. The concentration of flies is at the area between the dish machine and the area with and ice bin, glass sprayer, and dipper well. The dry storage area is free of flies at this time. The facility has regular pest control. Inspector highly suggests putting into practice the advice of the pest control operator. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the floor drain at the bar to still have some soil in it around the edge where the pipe changes diameter. Ensure that all the areas of the drain are clean. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Inspector observed both soda guns at the bar to be heavily soiled with mold. The same conditions existed at the last routine inspection on 9/8/23. Develop a habit of cleaning at the bar and maintaining the food contact surfaces properly cleaned and sanitized.
The soda guns were properly cleaned during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site.

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Inspector observed soda guns to be heavily soiled with mold. Soda guns are a food contact surface. Soda is contaminated with mold as it passes through the soda dispenser. Properly clean and sanitize this food contact surface at lest once every 24hours. 

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Inspector observed cranberry juice labeled must refrigerate after opening and ZingZang stored in the bar wine cooler. The items were 45F when checked with a probe thermometer. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection. Do not use the wine cooler for juices or any other food item. Only food items that do not require refrigeration should be stored in the wine coolers as they do not hold at 41F or below. The cranberry juice and ZingZang were discarded.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Inspector observed open cream in the bar glass front cooler lacking a date marking. Date all dairy and juice products. They are prepared,  TCS foods and require date marking. Cream was date marked. This is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Inspector observed drain flies at the bar and dry storage back by the onions. The facility has regular pest control. Look into more effective methods to rid the facility of drain flies. 

6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Caulking needs to be redone between the dish machine drain board and the wall. 

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Soda guns at bar are observed to have a mold growth on them. The soda dispensing guns were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. Properly clean and sanitize on a regular basis to preclude the growth of molds. The violation was corrected on site.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Cold brew coffee, labeled as perishable, and cranberry juice labeled must be refrigerated after opening along with a quart of half and half are observed to be stored in a wine cooler that is holding at 45F. The sided of the half and half container are swelling. Do not hold TCS (temperature control of safety) foods in wine coolers unless they are able to hold foods at 41F or below. Foods were 45F on the top rack. The foods were voluntarily discarded. The violation is corrected on site. Please ensure that the bar staff is aware of this needed adjustment to the current practice. Before inspector left, a member of the bar staff arrived for work and inspector was able to go over violations and corrective actions with him.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

A houe made pistachio coquito bottled at the bar bears a date of 8/11. Several bottles of Lavender syrup made of lavender flowers is labeled from April.  Label house made items and use or discard in 7 days. The coquito and lavender syrups were discarded at time of inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.comment:
3-302.12: If in working container, FOOD not readily recognized or easily mistakable shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. 

Several foods at the bar including cherries and syrups or mixes are unlabeled. Label working containers properly.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The bottom of the small wine fridge that was holding TCS items is heavily soiled with what appears to be spilled cold brew coffee. Also door seals of the units behind the bar are sticky. Clean and maintain clean for next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Observed an open bottle of Sprite in the reach in cooler across from the fryers. Also observed a bottle of Mr. Dew on the prep table in back. The bottles were removed. Store drinks in a manner to prevent contamination of food and food related items.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed a phone to be laying on a long cutting board where food was being prepared approximately 5 inches away. The phone was removed and the cutting board was sanitized per inspector direction. Do not have phones and personal items in the kitchen. Protect food prep surfaces.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

Observed two 2oz portions of crab to be in the prep top at 47F. These portions were stacked above the fill line on the pan. Also, some truffled goat cheese is 45F on top. Again, food was stacked above the fill line of the container. Facility states that items are kept in the tops of prep coolers over night.  Strongly suggest discontinuing this practice. Cover, date and move all items from prep tops to walk in cooler for overnight storage.  Portions of crab and top two inches of goat cheese were discarded in the garbage.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

Observed a wood shelf in the wait station between soda fountain and prep table to be absorbent/raw and no longer easily cleanable. Also shelves under bar have chipped paint. Seal these areas so that they are smooth, easily cleanable and nonabsorbent.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the metal shelving unit with the clean utensils to have a layer of dust/debris. Shelving units should be power washed. Clean cookware is being stored on top of the shelving units therefore contaminating food-contact surfaces. Discussed with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 10/7/22.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed several coolers to lack thermometers. Ensure extra thermometers are on site. Ensure thermometers regularly kept in all cold holding units. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed several area where plates and bowls were flipped upright therefore exposing food- and lip-contact areas. Flip over all single service items, plates, bowls, etc. Discussed with PIC. Area with prep cooler across from 3 compartment sink had the most plates/bowls not flipped over. 

Observed knives to be going in several directions within the knife basket (server area in front of prep line). Ensure knives are placed in a unison order to prevent touching food-contact surfaces of the knives. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs:
1. Caulking needs to be redone in the following areas: hand sink near the 3 compartment sink, hand sink near dish machine, dish machine to wall (mold). No caulking in the following areas: hand sink in the employee bathroom, hand sink at the bar. Caulk sinks to wall. Ensure the hand sinks in the kitchen have caulking within the interior creases of the hand sink as well as caulking the sink to the wall.
2. The shelving units within the walk-in cooler are rusted. Re-seal the shelving units and/or paint. 

Discussed repairs with PIC. Repair by next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed a large quantity of the food handler’s licenses in the folder to be expired. Ensure staff re-takes food handler’s course as needed to remain valid. Ensure new hires have a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC. Update public health folder.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed no allergen training certifications for CFPM’s. Provide copies for the public health folder. Discussed certification for the food protection manager’s with the PIC. Ensure by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed an employee to improperly wash hands - no barrier was used. Ensure proper hand washing techniques. Ensure a barrier such as a paper towel is used to turn off faucet handles to hinder cross contamination of hands. Discussed with employee. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine at the bar to have 0 ppm of bleach after multiple runs and multiple times testing. MJ Kellner was called to service. Cease use of dish machine until repaired. Utilize the 3 compartment sink at the bar. Inspector will follow-up on 3/7/21.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple working containers of quaternary ammonium to not be labeled. Inspector labeled spray bottles. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 1/22/21 and 9/24/21.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
5-501.17: A toilet room used by females shall be provided with a covered receptacle for sanitary napkins.

Observed no covered receptacle in the employee bathroom. Ensure a covered receptacle is provided for this bathroom before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

(REPEAT) Observed mops to not be air and/or drip drying. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to air and/or drip dry. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no policy for illness clean-up. Provided copy. Discussed hanging by mop area for clean-up. COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-201.11: (A)-(B) POISONOUS MATERIALS shall be stored to prevent contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES by separating or locating MATERIALS in area away or below FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES (use partition or store below). 

(REPEAT) Observed almost every sanitization spray bottle in the building to lack common name on bottle. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 1/22/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies. 

Observed both mops within mop buckets in the utility closet. Discussed proper mop storage with PIC. Ensure mops are hung in a manner that allows to drip and/or air dry. COS.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC.

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Provided new copies. Discussed with PIC regarding importance of document and that all food handler's must sign. Discussed keeping in the PH folder once signed. Inspector will follow-up on 2/1/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.

Observed CFPM to start cooking again without washing hands after walking with inspector throughout facility and performing other tasks. Food handler's must wash hands before engaging in food preparation or cooking. Discussed with CFPM. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.14: A sign or poster that notifies FOOD EMPLOYEES to wash their hands shall be provided at all HANDWASHING SINKS used by FOOD EMPLOYEES and shall be clearly visible to FOOD EMPLOYEES.

Observed multiple hand sinks throughout facility to lack hand washing signed. Provided new signs for facility. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed bleach at bar dish machine to be 0 ppm. PIC called MJ Kellner who arrived during inspection. MJ Kellner repaired dish machine. 200 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

Observed multiple milk jugs to be open and lack appropriate date marking. Milk jugs were discarded during inspection. Discussed proper date marking with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.comment:
7-102.11: Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

Observer sanitizer bottle to not have a label indicating substance. PIC wrote common name on the spray bottle. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

Observed back door near side server area to the right of the building to have seal coming away from exterior door (near bottom of door in corners). Replace door seal before next routine inspection in order to hinder pest access.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door.

Observed employee bathroom door to lack self-closing door hinge. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat from the inspection on 10/30/20.

findings.title: Garbage & refuse properly disposed; facilities maintained
findings.comment:
5-501.13: (A) Receptacles shall be durable, cleanable, insect- and rodent-resistant, leakproof, and nonabsorbent. (B) Plastic bags and wet strength paper bas may be used to line receptacles.

Observed hand washing station at wait server area to lack receptable. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat from the inspection on 10/30/20.
